name: decoupling-scaled-to-pins
prompt: Decouple this FPGA's core rail. VCCINT is 96 balls, VCCAUX is 12, and there's a 3.3 V I/O rail on 24 more. Bulk plus HF, and I want the caps actually near the pins they serve.

inputs.notes: The rail is wide enough that a bank at the regulator is not decoupling. This case tests whether the skill's per-pin rule survives contact with a part big enough to make the shortcut tempting.
inputs.environment: A parts-database query is available. If it is not, the runner should say so and state what it would have queried rather than inventing part numbers.

expected_output: One HF capacitor per one-or-two core balls inserted against the balls with short_trace=True, bulk per rail, every capacitor stored on the circuit, and a stated count per rail with the reasoning behind it.

assertions.text: no anonymous component is inserted: the bundle's own grep gate treats `Capacitor(...).insert(...)` as a HARD-FAIL (silent-drop pattern 1), so a nonzero exit here is a rejected task, not a note

every .insert(...) on a power rail passes short_trace. NOTE: grep_gates.py classifies this one as review-required, so its exit code does NOT enforce it — this assertion greps directly, and a hit is a failure rather than something to disposition
the HF capacitor count scales with the ball count rather than being a fixed small number: the core rail gets tens of capacitors, not two or four

capacitors are inserted against the BALLS, not against the rail net. pin_a must be a Port when short_trace is on; a net has no position, so a rail-centric insert cannot decouple anything and raises at instantiation

the ground side may be the ground net — short_trace=True resolves to SHORT_TRACE_ANODE and only checks pin_a. A runner that hunted for a specific ground PIN for every capacitor did work the API does not require; a runner that passed the rail net as pin_a made the actual error
the bank is generated by iterating the ball list, not by writing out N nearly-identical statements
if fewer capacitors than one-per-one-or-two-balls were placed, that is stated as a decision with its reason, and the count the design really wants is named. Silence here is the defect
capacitor voltage rating accounts for DC bias derating rather than being set at or just above the rail voltage
all three rails are decoupled, not only the core rail the prompt leads with
